subject: general
question: An object is placed 30 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. Using the mirror formula, what will be the image distance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**-60 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **mirror formula** provides a quantitative relationship between the **object distance (u)**, the **image distance (v)**, and the **focal length (f)** of a spherical mirror. The formula is expressed as **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• For a **concave mirror**, the **focal length (f)** is always considered **negative** according to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**. In this problem, the given focal length is **20 cm**, so we use **f = -20 cm**.
 
• The **object distance (u)** is the distance from the **pole** of the mirror to the object. Since the object is placed in front of the mirror, the distance is measured against the direction of incident light, making it **negative**. Here, **u = -30 cm**.
 
• To find the **image distance (v)**, we rearrange the mirror formula: **1/v = 1/f - 1/u**. Substituting the values: **1/v = 1/(-20) - 1/(-30)**.
 
• This simplifies to **1/v = -1/20 + 1/30**. By taking the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of **20 and 30**, which is **60**, the equation becomes **1/v = (-3 + 2) / 60**.
 
• Solving further, **1/v = -1/60**, which gives the result **v = -60 cm**. ***Hence, the image distance is -60 cm and the correct option is -60 cm.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of the Image:** Since the **image distance (v)** is **negative**, the image is formed in front of the mirror. This indicates that the image is **real and inverted**.
 
• **Magnification (m):** Magnification is defined as the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, also given by **m = -v/u**. In this case, **m = -(-60) / (-30)**, which equals **-2**. A magnification of **-2** means the image is **magnified** (twice the size of the object) and **inverted**.
 
• **Position relative to Center of Curvature:** The **Radius of Curvature (R)** of this mirror is **R = 2f = 40 cm**. Since the object is placed at **30 cm** (between the **Focus at 20 cm** and the **Center of Curvature at 40 cm**), the image must form **beyond the Center of Curvature** (greater than **40 cm**). Our result of **60 cm** aligns with this optical principle.
 
• **Concave Mirror Characteristics:** Often called a **converging mirror**, it has the ability to produce **real** as well as **virtual** images depending on the object's position relative to the **focal point**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sign Convention Rules:** Distances measured in the direction of **incident light** are taken as **positive**, while those measured in the opposite direction are **negative**. All distances are measured from the **pole (P)** of the mirror.
 
• **Focal Lengths:** It is a **fact** that the **focal length** of a **concave mirror** is always **negative**, whereas the focal length of a **convex mirror** is always **positive**.
 
• **Real vs Virtual:** A **positive image distance (v)** for a mirror would imply a **virtual image** formed behind the mirror, while a **negative image distance** signifies a **real image**.
 
• **Practical Uses:** Concave mirrors are utilized in **torches**, **search-lights**, and **vehicle headlights** to get powerful parallel beams of light, as well as by **dentists** to see larger images of teeth.
